label: early copy phase: outputting original tokens 1 and 2 (step right after first copied token)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, almost entirely on the first two steps after the delimiter step: recall_idx 1 (input is the first original token, prev input is <DEL>; 94% active, 80% of activation mass) and recall_idx 2 (70% active, 18% of mass). Rarely fires at recall_idx >= 3 (12% at 3, near zero beyond). Never fires in the original phase or on the <DEL> step itself. Magnitude is much larger at recall_idx 1 than 2, and larger for short sequences (all top examples are L=3, where the step is near the end of the sequence). Little token identity dependence (in_tok/out_tok lifts are flat).

issues: All factual claims hold on dev: active 0% in the original and delimiter phases. At recall_idx 1: 93.9% active, 80.5% of mass. recall_idx 2: 70.5% active, 18.1% of mass. recall_idx 3: 11.7% active, 1.2% of mass. recall_idx 4 and later: under 2% active. Top examples are all L=3. L=3 sequences hold 7.9% of mass on 1.2% of steps, and L=4 hold 30% of mass on 9% of steps. The in_tok and out_tok lifts are flat (about 1.1-1.4x and 2.1-2.5x across tokens).
Test scores reproduce: P 0.822, R 0.924, F1 0.870, mass recall 0.986.
Missed activations on test (67k steps, 1.4% of mass) are tiny trailing activations at recall_idx 3-4 (about 0.02-0.08 of max). This is scattered tail, not a separate class.

False positives are mostly recall_idx 2 in long sequences, and the effect is graded by length. Precision at recall_idx 2 is 0.85 for L<=5 and 0.65 for L>=7. Restricting recall_idx 2 to L<=5 or L<=6 cuts test F1 to 0.79 / 0.80, so the original predicate stays best.
recall_idx 1 non-firing (6%) skews somewhat toward digit first tokens in long sequences. Excluding that case does not help (test F1 0.845), so it is not a systematic class.
Minor wording: 'outputting original tokens 1 and 2' uses 0-indexed tokens, which matches recall_idx. The label does not overclaim relative to the predicate.
